media_strategy.selection_principle: Lean media budget by directive: at most one generated image (hero), no video, no music. Charts, CSS/SVG, and interactive HTML carry the rest. Channels are chosen data-first within those constraints.

chart.reason: The dataset is fundamentally quantitative: a decade trend, rankings, distributions, and a geographic ranking all map cleanly to charts.

image.reason: One cinematic hero image of the garage-to-skyline arc sets the founder-factory frame. Lean budget caps it at exactly one generated image.

video.reason: Lean media budget forbids generated video. No dataset moment requires motion that a CSS/SVG timeline cannot convey.

audio.reason: Lean media budget plus an abstract company-founding dataset: there is no sonic dimension, and a forced sonification of a 12-bar decade series would be decorative, not explanatory. Visual charts fully carry the patterns.

interactive_or_map.reason: The landmark timeline is an interactive scrubbable CSS timeline; the geography finding is rendered as an interactive Leaflet map of headquarters clusters. Both add exploration beyond static charts.

des_teaser.label: Hero image — garage to skyline

content.prompt: Cinematic wide editorial photograph: a weathered 1930s Palo Alto garage at golden hour dissolving into a modern Silicon Valley skyline, muted teal-and-amber palette, no text, no logos.

des_teaser.brief: Full-viewport hero image: a 1930s garage glowing at golden hour, its hillside dissolving into a modern tech skyline. Dark gradient overlay at the bottom so the headline reads cleanly. No text baked into the image. This is the visual thesis — the original garage startup and the empire it seeded, in one frame.
des_teaser.rationale: A single still image earns the one-image budget by carrying the entire arc of the piece (1939 garage to today's Valley). Video is barred by the lean budget and motion would add nothing here.

des_01.label: Most prolific founders bar chart (with Musk caveat)

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows founder and exact org count

style.palette: single muted teal, Musk bar in amber accent

des_01.brief: Horizontal bar chart of the top 12 founders by number of organizations founded, sorted descending. Elon Musk's bar (15) sits at the top, highlighted in the amber accent color while the rest are muted teal, with a small annotation note '~2 days at Stanford'. Y-axis = founder name, X-axis = org count. Hover shows exact counts. This visually plants the hook: the biggest bar belongs to the founder who barely attended.
des_01.rationale: A ranking with one provocative outlier is best shown as a sorted bar chart with the outlier highlighted, rather than a table.

des_02.label: Foundings-by-decade area/line chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows decade and count

style.palette: amber gradient fill under a teal line

des_02.brief: Filled area chart of unique organizations founded per decade, 1910s through 2020s. The curve climbs gently then surges to its peak of 120 in the 2000s (the 2000s point marked/annotated). X-axis = decade labels, Y-axis = count. The shape itself is the message: the rise of Silicon Valley as one line.
des_02.rationale: A time trend with a clear peak reads instantly as a filled area chart; the silhouette is the point.

des_03.label: Interactive landmark timeline (HP to Palantir)

content.initial_state: A horizontal axis from 1939 to 2003 with a node for each landmark company; the first node (HP, 1939) is expanded showing year, founder, and a one-line note.
content.trigger: Reader clicks or keyboard-arrows between nodes (or hovers on desktop).
content.transition: Selected node enlarges and its detail card slides in: company, founding year, founder shown, and a short context line (e.g. Sun = Stanford University Network).
content.payoff: Scrubbing from the 1939 garage to 2003 Palantir, the reader feels the canon as one continuous Stanford lineage.

des_03.brief: A responsive numbered-card timeline (NOT a fixed-width absolute layout) of the 11 landmark companies from ana_07's data_table. On desktop, a horizontal rail of year-stamped nodes the reader can click; on mobile, a vertical stack of numbered cards. Each card: big year, company name, founder shown, and a one-line context note for HP (garage), Sun (Stanford University Network pun, built from spare parts), and Cisco (router code from Stanford). Highlight HP as the origin. This is the page centrepiece.
des_03.rationale: The dataset's most emotionally resonant slice is a datable canon; an interactive timeline lets the reader walk the lineage rather than read a list, and avoids a third chart in a row.

des_04.label: Stat callout — 59% missing industry

content.label: of records don't say what the company even does

des_04.brief: Large 72px stat '59%' with the label 'of records don't say what the company even does (323 of 545)'. Placed as the honesty pivot at the top of the fog section, before the breakdown chart.
des_04.rationale: The missing-industry figure is the piece's turn; a single big number stops the reader before the chart explains it.

des_05.label: Industry coverage breakdown bar chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows count and pct

style.palette: muted, with 'No industry recorded' in a desaturated grey to read as a void

des_05.brief: Horizontal stacked or simple bar of the three coverage buckets from ana_05: 'No industry recorded' (323, 59.3%), 'Tech-flagged' (104, 19.1%), 'Industry given, not tech' (118, 21.7%). The grey 'No industry recorded' bar dominates, visually making the point that most of the data is a void. Hover shows count and percent.
des_05.rationale: Shows that the tech flag is a floor by making the missing-data bucket physically the largest bar.

des_06.label: Tech vs other (known-industry) split + named industries

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows industry and count

style.palette: tech-stack industries (software, computer hardware, artificial intelligence, information technology, Internet, semiconductors, software development, e-commerce) in teal; others in muted grey

des_06.brief: Horizontal bar chart of the top named industries from ana_04, sorted descending. Color tech-stack industries (software, computer hardware, AI, IT, Internet, semiconductors, software development, e-commerce) in the teal accent and non-tech (financial services, retail, film) in muted grey, so the reader sees the tech cluster light up. Pair with the prose stat that 88 of 202 known-industry companies (43.6%) are tech.
des_06.rationale: Once the fog is cleared, a colored ranking lets the tech bloc visually win without a separate donut chart.

des_07.label: Headquarters map (Leaflet)

content.initial_state: An interactive Leaflet/OpenStreetMap centered on the SF Bay Area, with circle markers sized by company count for each HQ city in ana_03's data_table.
content.trigger: Reader pans, zooms, and clicks a marker.
content.transition: Clicking a marker opens a popup with the city name and company count.
content.payoff: The cluster of large markers around Palo Alto / Mountain View / SF makes Terman's keep-them-near-campus legacy literally visible on a map; New York and D.C. sit far away and small.

des_07.brief: Leaflet map (OpenStreetMap tiles, no API key) with proportional circle markers for the 12 HQ cities in ana_03. Marker radius scales with company count (San Francisco 51 biggest). Inline the city lat/lng in the HTML. Popups show 'City — N companies'. Default view framed on the Bay Area but zoomable out to show NY (11) and D.C. (9). Fixed ~460px height, responsive width.
des_07.rationale: The data has real geography (named cities); a Leaflet map is the correct, non-fake spatial treatment and beats a bar chart for showing clustering.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial, restrained — warm amber accent on deep slate, serif body
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: text-first; each section states its claim in prose, then resolves into a chart, interactive, or map directly below
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Avoid a chart streak: the sequence alternates bar -> area -> interactive timeline -> stat+bar -> bar -> Leaflet map. No audio card, no video, no donut charts. The centrepiece is an interactive timeline, not a hero chart.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Large 72px stat callout for '59%'. Section titles in system-ui semibold; body in Georgia/serif. Subtle amber section dividers. Hero headline overlaid on the image with a dark bottom gradient.
